text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Newspaper headlines on the front page: State of emergency at the Democratic Party. 80,000 Vlore people welcome Romano Prodi. "Alba" arrives with hope for the Albanians. "Alba": Big landing today.
- Newspaper editorial says Europe is in dilemma over what to do with Albania's President Sali Berisha when the Albanian crisis is over.
- Arben Pasho, deputy prosecutor in southern Gjirokaster, said documents seized from General Ali Koceku dealing with the crushing of the revolt in the south charges senior officials of a grave crime.

- Italian PM Romano Prodi said during his last visit in Albania that operation Alba would be over in July; a joint committee for urgent assistance will be created, an Italian consulate to be opened in Vlore and Italy will consider the possibility for seasonal work for Albanian refugees.
- The Democratic party cannot be reformed as Berisha crushed the only constructive alternative within the party at a meeting of the leadership on Sunday, a newspaper commentary says.
- Prison officials say that only 60 out of 600 prisoners urged to return to jail have given themselves up.
- Bashkim Kopliku, a senior leader of the Democratic Party, says President Berisha last month ordered all party supporters to be armed.
- A "struggle" happened at the Democratic party and the chairmanship was changed while there were calls for Berisha's resignation.
- Former communist president Ramiz Alia, awaiting trial on charges of genocide and crimes against humanity, has left Albania.
- The party's national council held a meeting on Sunday to consider the recent unrest and map out what to do in the future.
President Berisha said fresh elections are the only way for democracy in the country.
- Vlore honours Albania by welcoming the Italian PM Prodi very warmly.
- An army officer said troops under the command of the head of the former secret police Bashkim Gazidede have bombarded Delvine.
